name: Illangelo
sources: Music Week — the team behind the sound (https://www.musicweek.com/publishing/read/living-for-the-weeknd-we-re-the-guys-behind-him-who-make-the-machine-work/064982)
notes: Alt-R&B/trip-hop sound designer, the "futuristic" half of the Toronto alt-R&B sound. The research folds the doubled reading itself: "the core alt-R&B mode is half-time (backbeat on 3) at 120—150 read as 60—75 felt", so `halfTime` is true at `halftime_3` and the encoded band is the felt spine, with the max reaching the stated 128 four-on-the-floor tracks. The drum block is the entry's and it is almost entirely about space: "the identity is space and reverb — a very sparse kick, a snare or clap pushed far back in a long hall, and reversed/gated percussion used as transitions rather than as a bed; hats are intermittent 16ths." So the kick density is 1—2, the snare carries a `large` reverb with a `soft` transient and the widest `layerClapOffsetMs` in this section (that is the hall), `hihat.continuous` is false at `fillDensity` 0.1, and `reverse` and `riser` lead the perc lanes because the entry says the percussion is a transition, not a bed. No `bass808` block: "deep sustained sub-bass tuned to the drone, plus distorted synth bass; the low end is continuous rather than rhythmic", which is a kick mirror at 0.92 with a low `anticipationProb` — a continuous low end does not lean far ahead of the beat — and no 808 is named. Harmony is "minor-mode and modal, with long unresolved suspensions and a static tonic drone; harmony is atmosphere first, function second", so `susSubstitutionProb` is 0.48, `maxChords` is 3, the tonic family carries weight and `chordDurationBeats` is the longest window authored here. "Loops are 4 or 8 bars and evolve by filter and reverb automation rather than by chord change" is why the melody phrase runs long and the counter is a smeared pad. ⚠ `confidence` is medium and the research says why: "the drum/reverb grammar is inferred from the records and marked". Every drum probability, the humanize numbers, the harmonic weights and `bpm.mode` 68 (the midpoint of the stated 60—75 felt band) are INFERRED. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 962/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** `melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.18 to 0.1. The counter's note count is `densityRatio` times the lead's own note count, so a bar the lead leaves empty is a bar the counter has nothing to answer — and one empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one, which is the single thing a seed cannot vary. Measured across this roster the models failing this gate average 0.150 here against 0.030 for the models that pass. ⚠ The value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "pads, processed guitar, tape-degraded samples and heavily effected vocal doubles form the palette; loops are 4 or 8 bars and evolve by filter and reverb automation rather than by chord change. Countermelody is usually a smeared synth or a reversed vocal.", and every claim in it still holds after the change. ⛔ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than `reese_sustain`, and that is an engine limit rather than a reading of the record.** `reese_sustain` is the only rhythm `bass.rs` reads that holds a note, and it emits one note per chord — TASK-162, still open — so this model measured **190 distinct basslines in 1,000 seeds** on it against `bass.rs`'s floor of 500. `mirror_kick` with a high root lock is the roster-wide substitution for a sustained sub (`dmx`, `coolio`, `krs-one`, `mobb-deep` all record the same one), and over a kick that plays a very sparse 1 and 3 it reads as held at this tempo. The research is *"deep sustained sub-bass tuned to the drone, plus distorted synth bass; the low end is continuous rather than rhythmic"*, which is exactly the shape TASK-162 has no rhythm for. ⚠ **INFERRED:** `followRootsProb` 0.92 and `anticipationProb` 0.18 are lane-conventional; the entry's own confidence line already marks the drum and bass grammar as inferred from the records. ⛔ **`cellShapes` came out (2026-08-17, bassline variety floor).** It was `[["1"], ["1", "5"]]`, and the first of those is the root and nothing else — a one-degree cell of the root says exactly what `followRootsProb` already says. `bass.rs` prefers a cell over `passingTones`, so half the seeds played every note on the root with `followRootsProb` unreadable, and neither half ever read the authored `P5`. Measured: **841 distinct basslines in 1,000 seeds**, a 0.841 share against `bass.rs`'s 0.95 — the lowest on the roster, and the reason is upstream of the bass: the kick this line mirrors is two anchored hits a bar that do not move with the seed, and the entry asks for exactly that (*"a very sparse kick"*). ⚠ Nothing sourced was lost: the fifth the cell reached for is still authored in `passingTones`, which is what the engine reads with no cell present. ⛔ **The repair took it to 905/1,000 and the floor is 950, and no honest lever is left.** The entry describes a low end with no movement in it — *"deep sustained sub-bass tuned to the drone, plus distorted synth bass; the low end is continuous rather than rhythmic"* — and the two parameters that would buy the share are the two the research pins: a lower `followRootsProb` is not *"tuned to the drone"* and a higher `anticipationProb` is not *"continuous rather than rhythmic"*, as the paragraph above already argues in the other direction. `reese_sustain`, the rhythm this entry actually describes, measures 190 in 1,000. Reported unresolved rather than bought. ⛔ The bassline declares `loopVerbatim`: the entry says "deep sustained sub-bass tuned to the drone, plus distorted synth bass; the low end is continuous", so this low end is static by description rather than thin by accident. `engine/tests/bass.rs::static_low_end` waives the saturation share for it and nothing else — the absolute floor of 500 distinct basslines still applies and this model clears it. The declaration needs the corroborating `followRootsProb` of 0.92 beside it, so the word alone could not buy the exemption.
